issues.issue: Compensating Interest is capped at the Servicing Fee for the related Servicer, but the proviso makes the Master Servicer liable "to the extent provided in Section 6.02(b)" without saying whether the same cap limits the Master Servicer's payment. Whether the Master Servicing Fee or the Servicing Fee bounds that backstop is left open.

The definition begins with an unnumbered clause for the Trustee and then a clause "(11)" for the Securities Administrator, and adds a third address "except for purposes of certificate transfer purposes." Which office is the Corporate Trust Office for a given notice or transfer is left to construction.

The Countrywide Servicing Agreement is described as being "between the Sponsor and Countrywide," while the Countrywide Assignment Agreement that assigns it to the Trust is among EMC, Countrywide and the Trustee. Which entity held the servicing agreement being assigned is inconsistent.

The Depository Agreement is described as "the agreement between the Trust and the initial Depository," although the Trust is not a contracting entity and the DTC letter of representations at Exhibit H is executed by the transaction parties. Who is bound by that agreement is unclear.

The Distribution Account is said to be created and maintained "pursuant to Section 5.08," but Article V contains no Section 5.08 and the Distribution Account is the subject of Section 5.02. The governing section for the account is misidentified.

The last sentence authorizes amendment of the rating requirements "[n]otwithstanding Section 12.01" and without Certificateholder consent, which cannot be squared with the amendment procedure and consent protections of Section 12.01. A court would have to decide which controls an amendment affecting account eligibility.

The carve-out excludes loans "purchased by the Sponsor, EMC or the related Originator pursuant to or as contemplated by Section 2.03," but Section 2.03 contains only Wells Fargo's own corporate representations; the repurchase machinery sits in Section 2.02 and the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement. The exclusion's reach therefore depends on reading Section 2.03 together with those provisions.

"Insurance Policy" is defined as "any insurance policy or LPMI Policy" and then as including "any replacement policy or policies for any Insurance Policies," a circular formulation with no limit on the kinds of policies captured. Whether a given policy is an Insurance Policy (and its proceeds Insurance Proceeds) is left at large.

Clause (e) captures interest on loans "repurchased by the Sponsor, Saxon (or its assignee), the Majority Class CE Certificateholder, or by the related Originator pursuant to Sections 2.02 and 2.03," omitting EMC, which is also a Seller obliged to repurchase under Section 2.02(c) and the definition of Seller. Interest recovered on an EMC repurchase is left outside Interest Funds.

Master Servicing Compensation is defined as the Master Servicing Fee "and any amounts earned on permitted investments in the Distribution Account during the Master Servicer Float Period," but the Master Servicing Fee definition already includes those same float earnings. The float income is counted twice.

The Master Servicing Fee is defined as a fee-rate calculation "and any amounts earned on permitted investments in the Distribution Account during the Master Servicer Float Period," which duplicates the second element of Master Servicing Compensation. The two definitions cannot both be given effect without paying the float income twice.

Maximum Probable Exposure is to be "calculated by the Depositor in accordance with the EMC's internal risk management process in respect of similar instruments," an external and undisclosed standard with no objective content. Nothing in the Agreement allows a reader to test the calculation.

"Mortgage" is limited to an instrument creating a "first lien on or first priority ownership interest" in the property, yet the pool expressly contains second lien Mortgage Loans (Mortgage Loan Schedule items (g) and (s), and the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement's definition of Mortgage Loans). On its face no second-lien instrument is a "Mortgage" for purposes of this Agreement.

A loan not in fact transferred remains a Mortgage Loan because of "a breach of the representation contained in Section 2.03(b)(v) hereof," but Section 2.03(b) is a one-sentence survival clause with no subsection (v) and Section 2.03(a)(v) is a consents representation by Wells Fargo. The cross-reference identifies no transfer representation.

The enumerated schedule fields use "(aa)" twice (for reset periods and for the Prepayment Charge) and contain several "[reserved]" gaps, so the lettering does not identify what the Mortgage Loan Schedule must contain. Which data the schedule must carry is a matter of construction.

The swap notional amount is said to be "set forth in the related schedule set forth in Exhibit M," but the Agreement has an Exhibit M-1 (Swap Agreement) and an Exhibit M-2 (Yield Maintenance Agreement) and no Exhibit M. Which schedule supplies the notional amount is unidentified.

The independence proviso disqualifies counsel connected with "EMC, the Depositor and the Master Servicer" only, although the opening sentence permits the opinion to be given by counsel for "the Seller," a defined term that also includes the Sponsor. Counsel for the Sponsor is thus permitted where independence was meant to be required.

"Optional Termination Date" is defined purely by a 5% balance test and not by any exercise of the clean-up call, and the definite article "[t]he Distribution Date" does not say whether it is the first such date or any date meeting the test. Because the Class A, M and B Pass-Through Rates step up "for each Distribution Date thereafter," the ambiguity directly affects coupon rates.

The first sentence excludes the Class CE Certificates from having a Pass-Through Rate yet lists "the Class CE Pass-Through Rate" among the applicable rates, and the second sentence then states the Class CE Certificate has no Pass-Through Rate. The definition contradicts itself as to that class.
